items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The band was what I just named: him and Nat, Sam Jones, Junior Mance, and me.

ctx.x: [Oscar] Pettiford. Pettiford’s band. He sat in with Pettiford, and Pettiford hired him. After that he played with Pettiford a little bit. He felt his way around. I think he got in touch with John Levy and told him he wanted to have a band. So he got a band and brought some guys from Florida that he had been playing with down there. They were, I think, Junior Mance, because they were – him and Nat was in the army with Junior Mance. And Sam Jones was there. He’d been – they had been playing with Sam. So it was…

items.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: I was with one of Cannonball Adderley’s first bands, him and Nat, and Junior Mance and Sam Jones and myself.

ctx.x: When is the singer coming on?

I’ll tell you another little thing. We had a band, I was with one of Cannonball Adderley’s first bands, him and Nat, and Junior Mance and Sam Jones and myself. So they used to play a little place in the town where Cannon was teaching school, called Porgy’s or Porky’s or something like that, the guy had a club, and they would go in and play. But Nat used to sing and it was Nat’s band, and Cannon was just in Nat’s band. Because Nat was a singer—

items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: We changed drummers a lot working with Cannonball, but Jimmy Cobb could handle it.

ctx.x: No, this is with Cannonball and Nat. The tune is called “Spectacular.”
[scats] “Spectacular” right, yeah. Jimmy Cobb on drums and Sam Jones. You know when that was? 1956. Forty something years, forty two years ago.

Man, I listened to that and I’m wondering if you ever were in a situation on a record like that and they’re counting off the tune like that, and you’re going, oh please, not that fast. That sounded awful fast to me.
